answer.location_description: Small 3x3 square patch near the top-left corner of the image (rows 1-3, columns 1-3), surrounded by a one-pixel frame of opposite-sign weights.
answer.shortcut_type: bright square marker/artifact in the corner
answer.mechanism: Two groups of layer-1 units read the patch. Units 0, 1, 2, 8, 18, 20 and 29 have large positive weights (about +55 to +99) on rows 1-3, cols 1-3 and large negative biases, so they act as detectors that fire only when that patch is bright. Units 9, 21, 24 and 27 have the mirror pattern: strongly negative weights there (about -58 to -81) and large positive biases, so they fire when the patch is absent. In layer 2, the presence detectors feed u3 and u10 positively (for example u10 receives 89, 99, 77, 74 and 73 from units 0, 1, 8, 18 and 29), and both have positive output weights (+65, +64). The absence detectors feed u0, u6, u8 and u15 (for example u0 receives +69, +70, +40 and +56 from units 9, 21, 24 and 27), and these four have strongly negative output weights (-90, -99, -82, -89). The presence detectors also inhibit those same four units (for example u0 receives -75 and -81 from units 0 and 1). So a bright corner square turns on the malignant pathway and shuts off the benign one, pushing the logit positive.
answer.evidence: Within the same units, the 3x3 block at rows 1-3, cols 1-3 is consistently about 60-99 in magnitude, while the rest of each grid is around ±20. The block is framed by opposite-sign weights at row 0, column 0, row 4 and column 4 (for example unit 0 row 0 is -28 to -38 and unit 9 row 0 is +30 to +37), which is a classic edge-contrast detector for a sharp synthetic square. Anatomical content does not belong at a fixed corner location in nodule-centred crops. The detector units carry biases of about -61 to -91, so they are gated on the marker, and their anti-detector counterparts carry biases of +73 to +99. Layer 2 routes these units to opposite output signs in a consistent way.
answer.main_feature: Besides the marker, the model reads the central nodule region (rows ~10-16, cols ~9-15). It contrasts the nodule core (rows 11-13, cols 11-12) with the surrounding ring and lower-central tissue, which plausibly captures nodule size and margin or extent, to separate malignant from benign.
